comment: Consumer-facing technologies are placed outside the architecture when they do not use shared health-system data. They may still influence care, create health data, trigger referrals, or later connect to DPI-H.

anchor.note: p.105 l.Lines 32-38 read as the printed page; section 5.1 agrees

public.text: Consumer-facing technologies are placed outside the architecture when they do not use shared health-system data. They may still influence care, create health data, trigger referrals, or later connect to DPI-H.
public.suggestedRevision: Clarify that such technologies may initially sit outside DPI-H but should become subject to applicable interoperability, safety, privacy, provenance, and data-quality requirements when they contribute information to or influence the health system.
